doc.title: Lorraine Feather interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, March 22, 2023

title: Growing up on Lambert, Hendricks & Ross and her father's circle
summary: She sang along with her mom to Lambert, Hendricks & Ross, met Jon Hendricks, and heard callers like Willie the Lion Smith and Andy Razaf.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Growing up with radio, records and family listening

blocks.x: Do you recall if your mother or if your father explained — tried to explain to you what Jon Hendricks and others were doing when they took those melodies that people had improvised and wrote lyrics. Did you understand that at that point?

No. I was never told what they did. It just was. It was just something that my mom and I used to try and sing along to with not very much success like Jackie. There’s the song about the mouse, the Annie Ross song, and everything. It was just so much fun. And I remember meeting Jon many times. He was a Virgo like me, he always used to bring that up. And I saw him perform — I saw him with Yolande Bavan who came after Annie Ross as you know. And it was just — it was just part of my musical life. It was some of the first music I ever glommed on to and thought was fun.
I love that vision. Like you know your classmates might have been singing [sings] Lollipop, Lollipop oh Lolli Lollipop, and you’re singing Lambert, Hendricks & Ross.
[Sings] The more I’m with you pretty baby. That’s “Centerpiece.” That was one of their slow tunes.
Yes. You know what Jon Hendricks called your father?
He told me “Learned Father,” yes that’s right.

Yeah, that’s right. I had kind of forgotten that but when you brought up Jon then I realized — and he asked me if I would like to be in his group, a later version of his group, many, many years later but it was just — it was driving around the country in a car and it was him and me and Judith and I think one of the participants, the singers, was going to be Bruce Scott who did sing with my vocal group for a while. He was really good at all that Lambert, Hendricks & Ross stuff. But yeah, I just — I never really thought about it but I heard nothing but that kind of music for years and years, Dinah Washington and of course Billie Holiday, Peggy Lee was my mom’s ex-roommate and friend. And it was just — it was just part of my life. The people who used to call the house were Willie “The Lion” Smith and he always introduced himself as, “Hello this is Willie ‘The Lion’ Smith. Can I speak to your dad?” And I was eight. I thought he was a real lion at the time.
Yeah he was. And Andy Razaf, the great lyricist who wrote with Fats Waller.
